name: S-300 (Soviet-legacy)

cost.display: Soviet-legacy stock; no current market unit price

characteristics: Strength: Very large pre-war stockpile; still forms a major share of Russia's IADS alongside S-400

Limitation: Older radar-guidance technology than IRIS-T-class IR seekers; some S-300 airframes have reportedly been repurposed for surface-to-surface strikes on Ukrainian targets, a role well outside its original air-defense design intent
Estimated quantity available: Large pre-war inventory (widely cited in the hundreds of launchers); current operational count not fully public
employment_notes: Same dual role illustrated on the Ukrainian side (S-300 repurposed for strikes) shows up independently in Russian use too — worth flagging in the Lessons Learned page as a cross-side pattern rather than a one-sided observation
contrast_vs_traditional: Both sides field descendants of the same Soviet S-300 lineage, and on the Russian side it is increasingly used for surface strikes against ground targets rather than the air-defense role it was designed for — existing inventory repurposed to a new mission because it's on hand, not because it's the doctrinally correct tool, a pattern that recurs across legacy Soviet-era systems on this battlefield.

notes: Rests only on tertiary reference works; wants a primary or trade source.
